jordan_cust: Hey team — we've got a production failure with tool/function calling. Calls to our `set_mode` tool started returning 400s this morning. Example error: `Invalid enum value 'AUTO' for parameter 'mode'`. This used to work with the OpenAI-compatible agent. cc @maria_support

maria_support: sorry you're hitting this, can you paste the full request body + model and a request id? Are you on Hosted or Dedicated? :thinking_face:

jordan_cust: Hosted API (using redwood's openai-compatible endpoint). request id: rq_3L9xQ. Minimal repro curl below: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/completions \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"set thermostat to auto"}],"functions":[{"name":"set_mode","description":"Set HVAC mode","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"mode":{"type":"string","enum":["OPEN_NOW","CLOSED_NOW"]}},"required":["mode"]}}],"function_call":{"name":"set_mode","arguments":"{\"mode\":\"AUTO\"}"}}'
```
Response from API: 
```json
{
  "error":{
    "message":"Function arguments failed validation","type":"invalid_request_error","param":"function_call.arguments.mode","code":"invalid_enum"
  }
}
```
This used to be accepted; OpenAI-compatible clients sometimes send `AUTO` or lowercase `auto`. Our front-end uses an enum helper that maps values, but the model sometimes emits `AUTO` and it breaks. We're seeing ~12% failures on the route and customers are hitting retries.

maria_support: thanks. that error implies the function schema enum in your `functions` list doesn't match what the model is emitting. We do have an OpenAI-compat layer but it doesn't currently normalize enum aliases automatically. tagging @devon_ml to confirm runtime behavior. I'll open an internal ticket. :white_check_mark:

devon_ml: @maria_support @jordan_cust quick notes: OpenAI's function-calling spec treats enum values as exact strings. Models sometimes generate tokens that are semantically equivalent but syntactically different (e.g. `AUTO`, `auto`, or `Auto`). Our current validator is strict and compares against the enum strings you declared (case-sensitive). Two options: 1) change your function schema to include all expected aliases in the `enum` array (e.g. `["AUTO","auto","Auto","OPEN_NOW",...]`), or 2) normalize `function_call.arguments` before validation (preferred). We should add a compatibility shim that does case-insensitive enum matching for string enums.

leo_eng: adding to this — runtime change required but low-risk: during parsing of `function_call.arguments` we can attempt to coerce enum strings by doing a case-insensitive match against the schema enum list. If there's an exact match after lowercasing, accept and coerce to the canonical enum value. I'll draft a patch. For immediate mitigation, jordan_cust can insert a proxy to rewrite `"AUTO"` -> `"OPEN_NOW"` if that mapping is deterministic.

support-bot: Ticket created: #SR-2349 (Tool-call enum mismatch causing function validator errors). Assigned to eng-runtime. Link: https://redwood.company/sr/2349

jordan_cust: We can't deploy a proxy quickly; can you provide a short-term config we can pass in the request to bypass strict enum validation? Our stack handles the function output (we call `set_mode` only), so relaxing validation server-side would be ideal. Also, will this cost us extra tokens (we're seeing retries) and is billing paused on failed calls?

maria_support: re: billing — failed calls that return 4xx still consume some compute but token billing is per-response; i'll check the exact billing behaviour for these error responses and confirm in the ticket. For bypass, we don't currently expose a request flag to disable enum checking (we validate the `function_call.arguments` to avoid bad downstream behavior). I'm going to ask eng if we can add a temporary query param `?compat=enum_aliases` to accept case-insensitive enum matches for a short window.

devon_ml: +1 on the query param approach for an emergency toggle. Implementation plan: accept `compat=enum_aliases` at the API layer, attempt to coerce enum strings (case-insensitive) and then run validation. If coercion succeeds, return success as though the argument matched. We should log a compatibility-warning for telemetry. Will need ~2-3 hrs to ship a small gateway change and runbook for rollback.

leo_eng: I'll prioritize. for reproducibility, can you attach a failing raw log from your end (request body we saw) and confirm the model variant (gpt-4o-mini in your example) and if you use function_call=\"auto\" or name specified as above? Also, are you using Redwood SDK or direct HTTP? If SDK, which version?

jordan_cust: attaching logs in the ticket (rq_3L9xQ). We're calling direct HTTP to the compat endpoint, no SDK. Model is `gpt-4o-mini`. We'll accept the compat flag for now. Any ETA? Our backlog is piling up.

maria_support: ETA for the compat query param: aiming for a canary release in ~3 hours, full rollout in ~6 hours if canary looks good. Engineer oncall: @leo_eng assigned. I'll follow up in the ticket with billing impacts and a recommended short-term mapping.

devon_ml: followup note — long-term we should also update our docs in "OpenAI compatibility" to warn about enum mismatches and provide recommended patterns: prefer explicit canonical enum tokens from the client, include aliasing in function schema if model output is uncontrolled, or use type=string + enum with more variants. Will add a docs PR.

jordan_cust: thanks team. please cc me on the ticket and share the compat flag API when ready. Also, can you confirm if tool selection (the model choosing which function to call) could be impacted by enum mismatch? We're seeing a few cases where the model chooses the wrong tool when enums fail validation.

leo_eng: good question — yes, function selection is upstream of argument validation. If the model emits a different argument string that makes the validator reject the function call, our fallback logic might retry the model or try a different tool variant depending on your route config. We'll include that behavior in the ticket and provide guidance to set `function_call` explicitly if you want deterministic selection.

support-bot: Update (#SR-2349): eng-runtime started canary for `compat=enum_aliases` on region us-west-2 at 1778007000.

maria_support: marking this thread as escalated to eng-runtime. will update here once the compat toggle is live and when we have billing confirmation. :shipit:
